Main work complete. All five required artifacts are produced in the workspace root: `analysis.py` (executed, self-contained, deterministic — byte-identical outputs on re-run), `poses.npy` [544,3], `loop_closure_scores.csv` (loop_id,false_probability), `metrics.json`, and `map_diagnostics.png` (hand-encoded PNG since matplotlib is unavailable offline; visually verified by decoding).

KEY FINDING — the plan-stage hypothesis was reversed by the data, and the reversal is decisively supported: the 55 loop candidates are NOT false. Forensics established that (1) poses_initial is exactly the odometry chain composition (max deviation 1.6e-8 m), (2) the edge sequence is self-similar in the local frame at lags {17,34,51,68,...} with the revisit period 68 = GCD of all 55 loop gaps (8 position-closure laps, total yaw ≈ 8.1·2π), (3) all 55 loops claim ≈0 relative displacement between poses 68k apart with measurement noise consistent with their stated sigmas (χ² vs the implied periodic configuration ≤ 20.9, 54/55 ≤ 8.5), and (4) poses_initial carries large piecewise-rigid per-lap drift: 6 of the 7 lap-boundary odometry edges have 7.7–18.3 m steps (vs 1.03 m mean) while their dθ stays ≈ +1.5716 rad. Under this reading the loop closures are the accurate measurements and the odometry chain is the drifted one; the alternative ("chain exact, all 55 loops false") is untenable because the 55 claims are mutually consistent at σ=0.075 precision with an exact 68-edge gap structure, and because the fold solution fits the joint graph at the noise floor.

SOLUTION (robust SE(2) pose-graph optimization, pose 0 anchored as world gauge, headings unwrapped internally / re-wrapped on output):
- Stage A coarse lap-graph alignment (21 params): the 8 recovered lap origins coincide within 0.105 m; χ² = 160.4 over 165−21 dof (χ²/dof 1.11) — independently confirms the periodic configuration.
- Stage B sparse Levenberg–Marquardt (analytic Jacobians, finite-difference verified to 8e-8) on 536 within-lap odometry edges + all 55 loops.
- Stage C robust GNC (Geman–McClure influence w=(μ/(μ+χ²))², μ annealed 1e3→30, weights refreshed each outer iteration) over ALL 598 edges — rejects the inconsistent edges without hand-picking; a degradation guard (revert-to-Stage-B) never triggered.
- Stage D hard inlier classification (χ²(3) 99% = 11.345) + final polish.

RESULT: χ² = 169.17 on 147 dof (χ²/dof = 1.15 — statistically consistent with the stated noise model). 537/543 odometry edges and 55/55 loops are inliers; the rejected edges are exactly 67,135,203,339,407,475 (translation residuals 8.4–17.4 m; edge 271 is retained because laps 3→4 carry nearly equal drift). Loop candidates were NOT rejected as false: per-loop final χ² ≤ 4.24 (median 0.83), and `loop_closure_scores.csv` false_probabilities span 2.3e-6…7.7e-4 (max 0.00077, loop 1) — all far below 0.5, i.e. every loop candidate is judged genuine; the actual inconsistent measurements in this graph are the 6 corrupted lap-boundary odometry edges. Per the requested cautions: metrics.json documents the kernel-sensitivity of the partition (GM/Cauchy agree with the primary partition, Jaccard 1.0; redescending Tukey variants destabilize and reject 3–13 good loops — recorded with per-kernel max χ²), the non-robust reference (all 598 edges, χ² = 22,672, dragged by boundary outliers), the all-loops-rejected reference (loop χ² = 1,239,395, min 234), and the chain-deformation statistics (mean correction 11.7 m, max 32.0 m, piecewise-rigid per lap: 1.0→19.5 m; within-lap relative geometry preserved to noise level; inconsistent with iid σ=0.0478/edge under either reading — the corrections are systematic drift, treated by robust re-weighting rather than σ inflation). A lap-coincidence diagnostic shows loop-covered phases agree across laps at RMS 0.19 m, while uncovered phases (64–67) spread up to 1.76 m — the irreducible √67-edge odometry random-walk uncertainty (0.55 m/axis) of the given graph, not an inconsistency.
